new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File present: (4 pp., text, SIL PNG Branch, created 2004-08-19; page header 'Ewage (Notu-Ewage, Notu) OPD Printed: August 20, 2004'). Fresh extracted text gives lines 21-22 exactly: 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' / 'The primary stress occurs on the first syllable.' - verbatim match to the compiler quote. Surrounding section: vowel-sequence note above, Syllable Patterns (V, VV, VVV, CV, CVV) below; no examples with stress marked, no tone or length statement, no noun/verb split, no secondary stress. Reading fixed: initial syllable is the only reading the sentence supports. Relation: the catalog has no record and no existing statement for ewag1241, so 'refines' (first statement held…
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no record and no existing statement for ewag1241, so this is the first stress statement held by the project: fixed initial primary stress. Direct SIL PDF link could not be reached by automated download (an automated-access block); obtained from the the Internet Archive capture of the same SIL URL (20240813205942).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the first syllable of the word; no tone or length contrast is mentioned under the suprasegmentals heading (the heading lists tone, stress, length but the only statement is about stress).
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned. The OPD is a 4-page datasheet: phoneme inventory, syllable patterns (V, VV, VVV, CV, CVV), orthography, a recorded passage; it gives no examples with stress marked and no verb/noun distinction.
new_statements.identity_note: Both works describe Notu-Ewage (Ewage, Notu) [nou] of the coastal strip between Bakumbari and Pongani, Oro Province; the OPD header names Popondetta district and villages Emo, Waima, Beama, Eroro, Garuro, Buna, Garawa, Gona, Pangani, Bakumbari. The grammar MS (p. 1.4, p. 5) notes that villages bordering the Korafe area are also Notu-Ewage speaking but that dialect differences had not been studied; neither work specifies a dialect for its data. Smallhorn 2011 notes the name 'Ewage' ('salt-water talk') also covers other Notu groups.

sources.note: Comparative phonology sketch and Notu wordlist; stress mentioned only for Suena (p. 69: 'tone is separate from stress and may well be phonemic') and for King's Binandere dictionary (p. 74: 'There is no tone or stress analysis.. /ewa/.. a minimal pair of stress/tone'). Nothing on Notu stress. (The penultimate-stress sentence in the same PL A-18 volume, p. 90, belongs to Wilson's 'Suena phonology', not Notu.)
